findings.description: The site footer on the French landing page is left entirely in English, identical to the English version, instead of being translated.
The full name field validation error on the French apply form is shown in English, while all other field errors on the same form are correctly translated to French.

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande pour 5 000,00 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: On the French application confirmation page, the template placeholder {montant} is shown literally instead of being replaced with the formatted loan amount, unlike the English version which correctly shows $5,000.00.
The "Recent transactions" section heading on the French dashboard is left in English instead of being translated.

Transaction dates on the French dashboard are shown in US MM/DD/YYYY format (e.g. 09/15/2026), while the English version correctly uses ISO format (2026-09-15). This is not a valid fr-CA date convention and is ambiguous/wrong.
On the French dashboard, the "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link incorrectly points to the English calculator page (/en/calculator) instead of staying in French (/fr/calculator).

The "Pay later" checkbox option on the calculator is translated as "Payer maintenant" (Pay now), reversing the meaning. A user enabling this option in French would believe they are choosing to pay now, the opposite of the actual deferred-payment feature.

The estimated monthly payment on the French calculator page is shown using US currency formatting ($450.91) instead of the Canadian French convention (450,91 $), unlike other amounts on the site such as the dashboard balance which correctly show "12 458,30 $".

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve de l'approbation du crédit.
findings.description: The French rate note drops the qualifier "subject to credit approval" that is present in the English version ("Variable rate of 5.2%, subject to credit approval.").

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais ne s'appliquent pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Accusation" means a legal accusation in French, not a monetary charge/fee. This mistranslates "No charges apply for early repayment" with an incorrect and confusing word.
The modal's "Close" button is mistranslated as "Proche" (a false friend meaning "near/nearby"), instead of the correct French term for closing a dialog, "Fermer".

findings.observed: Image (promo-c.png) displays "Taux fixe : 4,9 %" while its alt text says "Taux variable : 5,2 %"
findings.expected: Image should display "Taux variable : 5,2 %" matching the English version's promo-a.png which shows "Variable rate: 5.2%"
findings.description: On the French calculator page, the promo banner image shows completely different text ("Taux fixe : 4,9 %" / Fixed rate 4.9%) than its own alt attribute ("Taux variable : 5,2 %") and than the equivalent English image (promo-a.png, "Variable rate: 5.2%"). A different, mismatched image file is being served for the French locale.

The landing page subtitle uses the informal "tu" form (Découvre, tes), while the rest of the application (e.g. apply form validation "Vous devez donner votre accord...") consistently uses the formal "vous" register expected for a bank.

The field label uses the anglicism "e-mail" while the validation message for the same field correctly uses the Quebec French term "courriel" ("Entrez une adresse courriel valide."), creating inconsistent terminology.
"Balance" is an anglicism when used for an account balance in French; the correct banking term in Canadian French is "solde". "Balance" properly refers to a weighing scale.

The application confirmation page served at a /fr/ URL declares its document language as English ("en") instead of "fr-CA", even though all other French pages (landing, apply, calculator, dashboard) correctly declare lang="fr-CA".
